name: bm-v1-stage1-modulus-remodelling
claim: A coarse-grained collagen IV network (two-bead rods, stochastic NC1/7S crosslinks, no excluded volume) run through the spec's stage-1 protocol — stretch, hold, then switch the chemistry on — yields a separable elastic modulus and remodelling (stress-relaxation) time on real LAMMPS.
experiment: Build N two-bead rods in a quasi-2D periodic slab; assemble a crosslinked network with fix bond/create (NC1 binds 1, 7S binds 3); equilibrate with the chemistry frozen; apply an equibiaxial in-plane strain (fix deform) with the chemistry frozen (elastic loading); hold and read the elastic plateau; then switch crosslink make/break on and read the viscous stress relaxation. Network stress is the bond-virial pressure only (no kinetic term), normalised by the initial volume — the spec flags the all-atom stress as a stage-1 error.
result: Runs end-to-end in ~4 s. The network assembles ~100 crosslinks from 200 rods, the stress-strain ramp gives a positive but very soft tangent modulus (~0.3–0.8 in LJ units, ~1–2 Pa at kT/a³ ≈ 2.5 Pa) consistent with the paper's ≈0.03 Pa linear modulus, and the chemistry-on hold shows a stress change as crosslinks turn over. The remodelling time is currently noise-limited at this network size (flagged, not silently zeroed) — calibration is spec decision #10.

purpose.question: Can the clean-room collagen IV network separate an elastic modulus from a viscous remodelling time, as the paper's staged protocol does?
purpose.mechanism: A crosslinked semiflexible rod network stores elastic energy in stretched bonds under fast load (crosslinks frozen), and dissipates it over the crosslink turnover time when make/break is switched on.
purpose.expected_outcome: A finite, very soft elastic modulus and a stress-relaxation time set by the crosslink kinetics (MP), calibratable to the ≈20 h collagen IV lifetime.

key_assumptions: One protomer = one two-bead rod; junction flexibility folded into a finite intra-rod bond (dynamic junction angles omitted in v1-minimal).
No excluded volume — every pair coefficient is zero (spec #2: the released decks set eps=0).
Crosslink make/break locked at FactorMult = 0.66 (make/break ratio 1.52), as in the released decks.
Quasi-2D slab; rods lie in-plane; thickness/layer count deferred (spec #9).
Energy unit = kT, so stress unit = kT/a³ ≈ 2.5 Pa; absolute pascals not yet claimed (spec #4).

if_primary_tests_pass.implementation_status: Stage 1 runs end-to-end and separates elastic from viscous.
if_primary_tests_pass.biological_validation: Qualitative match to the paper's very-soft regime; absolute Pa gated on the energy-scale decision.
pipeline_unblocks: Stage 2 — σ(ε̇) sweep on the growing (biaxially stretching) substrate.

diagnose: Network under-percolated — raise make_prob or assemble length.
Stress noise-dominated — larger network / seed ensemble.
Bond-virial stress readout — confirm the kinetic term is excluded and V0-normalised.
if_primary_tests_fail.block_downstream: Do not proceed to stage 2 until stage 1 gives a stable modulus.

limitations: Very small network (200 rods) — the relaxation signal sits near the thermal-noise floor; τ needs a larger network / seed ensemble.
No dynamic junction angles; persistence length is only approximately represented (spec: LAMMPS puts l_p as soft angles at junctions).
No excluded volume, so pore-size / bundling readouts are not yet physical (deferred).
Modulus reported in LJ units / as a ratio, not calibrated pascals (spec #4).
Parameters transcribed from the spec's sheet, NOT the authors' actual decks (not yet in hand).

report.title: Stage 1 — collagen IV modulus & remodelling (clean-room v1)
report.verdict: The staged protocol runs on real LAMMPS and separates a (very soft) elastic modulus from a crosslink-turnover stress change. Absolute stiffness and a calibrated remodelling time are gated on the open energy-scale and calibration decisions.
report.main_insight: A clean-room coarse-grained collagen IV network reproduces the paper's qualitative regime — a network dominated by crosslink pre-stress with a very soft strain response, consistent with the published ≈0.03 Pa modulus.
report.caveat: Parameters are transcribed from the spec, not the authors' decks; the network is small and the relaxation signal is noise-limited.
